correctness.rationale: All path copies on a given bipartition-size pattern have equal multiplicity; this yields exact transition \(p=(a-r)/(a+b-2r)\). The deterministic even-path count is exact. For odd k, gamma-ratio normalization makes the imbalance a martingale; predictable quadratic variation tends to \(1/(k-2)\) times N, with small late-stage tail because 2/k<1 and martingale jumps \(o(\sqrt N)\). The terminal min-class barrier differs from |D|=S by at most 2r, yielding the powered normal law. Macroscopic imbalance follows from the same martingale uniformly away from the boundary. The actual package checker passed 11 exhaustive labelled-state comparisons, 564 rational drift tests, 6300 even stoichiometric identities, and six exponent identities. No finite experiment was used to prove an infinite limit.

value.rationale: The result classifies a natural physical stoichiometric parity effect: odd alternating molecules amplify randomness into \(N^{\theta}\) terminal vacancies even on balanced substrates, while even molecules give bounded deterministic defects. It quantifies the critical imbalance window with an explicit noncentral powered-normal law for every odd path length \(k\ge5\), and proves positive macroscopic kinetic waste on a substrate with an exact full packing. This is a general structural result and a qualitative parity distinction, not a one-parameter recomputation or mere simulation.
